newsitem.title: USA: Ride sees Q4 loss $0.20-$0.22/shr. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ride sees Q4 loss $0.20-$0.22/shr. [CORRECTED 23:00 GMT]

text.p: Ride Inc said Monday it would take $9 million in restructuring and write-down charges in the fourth quarter and expects to post a loss of $2.2-$2.4 millin, or $0.20-$0.22 per share, for the period.
A year earlier it reported a net profit of $1.87 million, or $0.16 per share.
Sales for the fourth quarter are expected to be between $13 million and $15 million, versus $25.7 million a year earlier, it said.

"We continue to have excess inventories, due primarily to canceled commitments from a Japanese distributor and from an oversupply of snowboards from other manufacturers," Ride Chief Financial Officer Scott Stewart said in a statement.

"As a result, we are writing down our inventories to reflect their lower value as close-out items," he said. "In addition, we are taking non-recurring restructuring charges which primarily relate to recent changes in our production of bindings, including the move of binding production out of our Preston, Wash., facility."
All but $350,000 of the charges are of a non-cash nature and relate to asset write-downs rather than cash outlays, the company said.

Ride said net income for the full year 1996 is expected to be $700,000 to $900,000, or $0.06-$0.08 per share, compared to 1995 net income of $5.95 million, or $0.57 per share. (Company corrects 1996 projection)

It said the projections include about $600,000 in transition management expenses, which consist primarily of an unspecified amount of severance compensation in the fourth quarter and about $1 million for the full year.
The results will also include a $500,000 gain from the sale of the closeout and brokered O.E.M. business segments of the company's C.A.S. Sports subsidiary.

"While sell-through of Ride's products appears to be favorable, excess inventories throughout the snowboard industry from oversupply has led to discounting, putting strong pressure on gross margins in the fourth quarter," President and Chief Executive Robert Hall said in a statement.

"We continue to see rapid consolidation taking place in the industry, with smaller competitors losing market share to the more dominant players," he added. "With our overall No. 2 market position, a strong balance sheet and our restructuring behind us, we believe that Ride is firmly positioned as a leader in this growing market and is well prepared to take advantage of the opportunities we see emerging from the ongoing industry consolidation and growth."
